messages.subject: Undo binwidth specification
parts:
Hi all:

I have been messing around with graphic options and came across
overlaying histograms with ggplot.

However, I assigned a binwidth of my data to 0.5 and want to undo that
operation. I know how to easily go to the command and change the
binwidth specification, but I would like to remove this specification
all together. Using boxplot functions allow data to be projected on
the fly taking into consideration the quartiles without specifying a
binwidth. Is this possible??


Thanks

Ty

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Undo binwidth specification
parts:
Hi:

I have to confess I don't understand precisely what you're asking...

On Sat, Oct 6, 2012 at 3:43 PM, Tyler Beeton <tybe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all:

I have been messing around with graphic options and came across
overlaying histograms with ggplot.
Overlaying histograms with what? An estimated density curve would be an initial guess, but not a unique one.

However, I assigned a binwidth of my data to 0.5 and want to undo that
operation.  I know how to easily go to the command and change the
binwidth specification, but I would like to remove this specification
all together.  Using boxplot functions allow data to be projected on
the fly taking into consideration the quartiles without specifying a
binwidth.  Is this possible??

Perhaps a violin plot would be of interest to you. Its outer boundary, symmetric about its center, consists of a kernel density plot, but is designed such that one can embed a boxplot inside it. See its help page if that interests you. If not, perhaps you should focus the question a bit more.

Dennis


Thanks

Ty
